title: I made a simulator where you trade the FTX crash candle by candle, without knowing what comes next
author: dmiseev

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: the look-ahead you can't remove is the menu. the moment someone picks "FTX crash" they know the direction and roughly the size, so what the sim really tests is nerve and sizing, not reading the tape. mixing in a few events that fizzled, a scary candle that went nowhere, would make the pick itself blind and the result a lot more honest.

replies.author: dmiseev
replies.body: fair, once you click "FTX crash" you already know which way its going, so yeah at that point its more nerve and sizing than reading the tape. thats kinda why blind mode is separate, random coin and date and you only find out what it was at the end. but the events list has exactly the problem you describe. mixing in a few scary candles that went nowhere is a good idea, writing that down

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: then blind mode is the real product and the events list is the tutorial. I'd put blind first on the menu and keep the named events as a replay you unlock after, because the first thing a trader does with a known crash is size up, and that habit is the one the sim should be breaking.

replies.author: dmiseev
replies.body: yeah thats a fair way to put it. the events list is what gets people in the door tbh, nobody clicks "random coin random date" as their first thing. but blind as the default with the event name as the reveal at the end is kinda the same idea from the other side. gonna play with that ordering

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: makes sense, the named list earns the first click and blind mode earns the second. I'd play it either way round.
